text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Northern areas of Namibia could face serious floods emanating from southern Angola.
- President Sam Nujoma has attacked corruption, graft and inefficiency and urged government officials to keep their backyards clean. Nujoma spoke at the opening of parliament yesterday.

- Electricity consumers in Namibia might have to pay more for power to finance the proposed hydro-electric power scheme at Epupa. According to a senior NamPower executive it is possible that electricity prices may have to be increased to finance the controversial project.

- President Sam Nujoma practiced restraint when opening parliament yesterday, opting for general observations in his speech to mark the occasion. He said that democracy had become a hallmark of Namibian society, but warned that political stability would be meaningless without real change in the lives of the people.
- The First National Bank of Namibia has issued fourty-four million shares of N$3.80 each to be sold from today.
